name: Brazoria Interconnector Gas Pipeline (BIG)
researcher_notes: The Brazoria Interconnector Gas Pipeline is an existing 42 inch gas line in Brazoria County, Texas. A World Pipelines article from January 2015 says it runs 30.5 miles from Stratton Ridge in the south to a point near Iowa Colony in the north. It is not the 10.6 mile Freeport LNG Train 4 feed line (existing row P3666) and not the 0.5 mile Stratton Ridge row (P1297). A 2019 federal order on the Freeport LNG Train 4 project lists the Brazoria Interconnector Pipeline as one of the lines that feeds the Stratton Ridge Meter Station, separately from the new 10.6 mile line. The Energy Information Administration project table for August 2026 (sheet Historical Projects, Excel row 497) lists it as a completed 2008 intrastate expansion in Texas, 30 miles, 42 inches, with 2,600 million cubic feet per day of added capacity. The consolidator note says it runs to Freeport LNG, but the source says it ends near Iowa Colony, so the endpoint follows the source. Start year 2008 comes only from the EIA table (April 2008 in service date). It is intrastate, so no federal filing is expected. Owner left blank on purpose. ConocoPhillips owned it. Spectra Energy agreed to buy it in January 2015 for the Texas Eastern Stratton Ridge Project, and a web search points to Enbridge as the current parent, but no loaded source confirms the closing or current owner. The EIA table names Freeport LNG Development LP, which conflicts. Capacity left blank because the sources give 1.8 billion cubic feet per day (2015 article) and 2,600 million cubic feet per day (EIA), they disagree, and the sheet has no billion cubic feet per day unit. The route was not researched. Length of 30.5 miles is above the 15.5 mile threshold. The 2019 federal order was checked for the pipeline name only and is cited in no field. Tier is high for existence, length and diameter, with two independent sources.
